## Top stories

- **HSC Exam Results Scheduled for October 29**: Results for the HSC and equivalent examinations will be officially published on October 29. Further details regarding the result publication will be shared on October 26 (বাংলা টেলিগ্রাফ, প্রথম আলো, The Business Standard).
- **Bangladesh Bank Takes Website Offline Amid Cyber Alert**: Bangladesh Bank has kept its official website offline following a global cyber alert to protect its systems (The Daily Star).
- **US Considers Iran Action as Tensions Escalated**: US President Donald Trump announced that the US is considering a possible attack on Iran as early as Sunday, while also noting that a major deal could still be reached with Tehran (Al Jazeera). Meanwhile, Iran blamed the US for previous deal failures and warned that even limited strikes would draw a far stronger response (Al Jazeera).
- **BSEC Reopens Direct Stock Exchange Listing Route**: Large private companies in Bangladesh are now permitted to list existing shares directly on the main boards of local stock exchanges without undergoing an initial public offering (IPO) under new rules from the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission (The Daily Star - Journalism without fear or favour).
- **BBC’s Blue Planet III Rejects AI Perfection**: The upcoming nature series *Blue Planet III* is intentionally retaining unpolished and flawed shots to maintain visual authenticity. Creators noted that hyper-polished footage has become a hallmark of AI-generated content (The Verge AI).
- **Hong Kong Launches 400 Fully Funded PhD Fellowships**: A total of 400 fully funded PhD fellowships worth HK$344,400 annually have opened for applicants of all nationalities in Hong Kong (Global South Opportunities).

## AI

- Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed the Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Advertising Act, mandating disclosures on AI-generated or heavily modified text, audio, image, and video advertisements (The Verge AI).
- TechCrunch published a tracker of failed or delayed AI projects, highlighting issues such as repeated delays to Apple's Siri AI and OpenAI's troubled "super app" rollout (TechCrunch AI).
- Producers of *Blue Planet III* are leaving imperfect footage in the final edit to distinguish real wildlife shots from overly polished AI visuals (The Verge AI).
- Research published on arXiv highlights why language generated by artificial intelligence remains uniquely difficult for humans to comprehend (Hacker News).
- Financial analysis indicates that there are currently no clear signs of financial payoff from AI investments outside of the core tech sector (Hacker News).

## Business

- Volkswagen's Audi division plans to build a factory in Georgia, USA, to offset heavy losses caused by US tariffs on European and Mexican imports (NYT Business).
- UK Chancellor's upcoming budget will feature a major devolution package aimed at giving local English leaders broader spending powers (The Guardian Business).
- Ukraine’s military confirmed a stable connection to SpaceX's Starlink system following recent usage restrictions, despite allegations from Elon Musk that terms of service were breached (The Guardian Business).
- Off the coast of Scotland, operations continue on an untapped oil field vessel in Rosebank while political debates over its future continue (BBC Business).

## Tech

- Google has officially withdrawn support for certain Nest smart thermostat models, reverting them back into basic, non-smart devices (Hacker News).
- The Danish government silently abandoned a trial program that aimed to replace Microsoft Office with open-source software alternatives across government departments (Hacker News).
- MIT highlighted Argus, a free open-source agentic security operations platform created to automate security workflows (Hacker News).
- The PHP Foundation is operating under significant under-funding with only one full-time employee on staff, according to its director (Hacker News).
- Software discussions focused on the newly developed Goose programming language, as well as Bbtree, an implementation for fast ordered maps (Hacker News).

## Bangladesh

- Bangladesh maintained its status as the top denim supplier to the European Union during the first eight months of 2026, despite experiencing an overall decline in export volume to the bloc (The Daily Star - Journalism without fear or favour).
- IT exports grew by 9% in FY2025-26, though industry leaders expressed concern that AI automation could threaten traditional Bangladeshi outsourcing work (The Daily Star - Journalism without fear or favour).
- Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury announced plans to bring the creative economy into mainstream national development (BD Bulletin, The Daily Star - Journalism without fear or favour).
- Biman Bangladesh Airlines will double its weekly flights on the Dhaka-Narita route starting October 29, coinciding with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s official visit to Japan (The Daily Star - Journalism without fear or favour).
- Japanese automakers are evaluating opportunities to set up local vehicle and parts manufacturing plants in Bangladesh (The Daily Star - Journalism without fear or favour).
- Over 22,000 Bangladeshi passengers suffered severe travel disruptions after 144 flights were canceled or suspended due to operational restrictions at Saudi airports (প্রথম আলো).
- The first unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant is conducting preparation tests ahead of its power startup (Bangladesh Post).
- Hefazat-e-Islam demanded institutional and legal punishment against moral degradation within educational institutions (প্রথম আলো).
- Religious festivals were celebrated across Bangladesh, including Lakshmi Puja (প্রথম আলো) and the Buddhist festival of Provarona Purnima (প্রথম আলো).

## Education & Admission

- HSC and equivalent examination results will be published on October 29, with detailed procedural notices set to be released on October 26 (বাংলা টেলিগ্রাফ, প্রথম আলো, The Business Standard).
- A ongoing stalemate regarding the Vice-Chancellor position continues to disrupt operations at Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET) (The Daily Star).
- Vietnam's Ministry of Education and Training proposed lowering priority points for 10th-grade admissions and requested feedback on limiting 10th-grade entrance exams strictly to Literature and Mathematics (Vietnam.vn).
- Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel delivered an address at the first convocation ceremony of KN University (Big News Network.com).

## Scholarships

- **Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme**: Offers 400 fully funded PhD fellowships worth HK$344,400 per year, open to international applicants of all nationalities (Global South Opportunities).
- **University of Twente Scholarship 2027**: Provides €22,000 in funding for international Master’s degree students studying in the Netherlands (Global South Opportunities).
- **Oxford African Studies Visiting Fellowship 2027-28**: Applications are open for fully funded fellowships targeting Sub-Saharan African scholars at Oxford University (Global South Opportunities).
- **18th CREEW Research Grant Program 2026/2027**: Research grant opportunities are open for eligible applicants (Global South Opportunities).

## What to watch

- **HSC Results Release**: Key procedural announcements on October 26 leading up to the official HSC exam results publication on October 29 (বাংলা টেলিগ্রাফ, প্রথম আলো).
- **US-Iran Security Situation**: Potential US military moves or diplomatic deal announcements regarding Iran over the weekend (Al Jazeera).
- **Prime Minister's Visit to Japan**: PM Tarique Rahman's official visit to Japan starting October 29, coinciding with expanded Biman flight services to Narita (The Daily Star - Journalism without fear or favour).
- **Global Elections**: Final run-off outcomes in Brazil's presidential election and developments in Israel ahead of upcoming national voting (Al Jazeera, BBC World).
